extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, editors, and literary critics (readers of the 1916 Yearbook / contributors to magazines)
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-evaluation criteria for American short stories (as used in a 1916 Yearbook: editorial summaries identifying what makes a story notable). Focuses on craft elements such as economy, characterization, plot, atmosphere, style, and artistic goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of means / suppression of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses rigorous economy and suppresses unnecessary detail to solve a noteworthy problem or achieve artistic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "With rigorous economy of means and suppression of detail, a noteworthy problem is solved in a superb work of art." Example praise: 'The Sacrificial Altar' is commended for this. Anti-pattern: wilful verbosity or over-detailing that dilutes the central problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine psychological insight and reticence
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrays characters' inner life with keen psychological penetration while maintaining restraint and reticence in exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "portrays with fine psychological insight and reticence the spiritual reactions..." Example: the French novelist in 'The Sacrificial Altar.' Value: insight without over-explaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of sentimentality while conveying warmth
rubrics_metrics.description: Conveys warm, tender human feeling or sentimental subject-matter without lapsing into mawkish sentimentality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "The temptation to sentimentalize a sentimental subject is tremendous, but ... has succeeded in clothing his story with sentiment, while completely avoiding sentimentality." Examples: 'Miss Willett'; watch for softness that becomes cloying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization by suggestion/dialogue rather than direct statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveals character indirectly—especially through dialogue and small detail—rather than through overt descriptive statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "suggestion in dialogue is substituted for descriptive statement." Example: Francis Buzzell's method in 'Ma's Pretties.' Anti-pattern: heavy-handed authorial exposition of character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion for etched background and salient human portrayal (character over event)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritizes finely drawn background and human portrayal over plot-driven events; emphasis is on character moments and milieu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "a passion for etched background and salient human portrayal rather than for event or sustained situation." Example: 'Supers' — craftsmanship resides in background and human portrayal rather than plot complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative power and atmospheric sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a persuasive atmosphere and displays imaginative vigor that immerses the reader in mood and setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "persuasively set forth with imaginative power and a fine atmospheric sense." Example: 'Fog' praised for atmospheric realization. Anti-pattern: flat or clichéd openings that weaken atmosphere (noted as possible but forgivable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid personification and descriptive coloring
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses personification and rich descriptive touches to conjure an atmosphere or setting with vividness and memorable color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "The atmosphere of the story is as vividly conjured up by personification... and the rich coloring of Mr. Cobb's descriptive touches is memorable." Example: 'The Great Auk.' Avoid underdescribed or generic narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision vs. verbosity (economy of narrative force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintains concision and selective power; avoids verbosity, reiterated monotony, or unnecessary stylistic excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "serious faults of style and a certain wilful verbosity" and "defect is a lack of economy and selective power." Example critique: Dreiser's 'Lost Phoebe' has verbosity; Fannie Hurst's stories sometimes lack economy. Scoring note: economy is a recurring defect even in otherwise strong work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in plot and carefully handled suspense / unforeseen denouement
rubrics_metrics.description: Displays originality of plot idea, manages suspense carefully, and delivers a natural but unexpected dénouement within a compact structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "reveals striking originality in plot, adequate characterization, carefully handled suspense, and a natural though completely unforeseen denouement. Its compactly wrought structure is a triumph of successful technique." Example: 'The Cat of the Cane-Brake.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration (fusion) of plot, characterization, atmosphere, and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieves a harmonious fusion of plot construction, character work, atmosphere, and stylistic control to produce a fully realized story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "fusion of plot and characterization in a fully realized picture cannot be studied to better advantage." Example: 'Down on Their Knees.' Scoring note: excellence often comes from balance across these elements rather than strength in only one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic dialogue and subtle character definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Employs dialogue with fidelity to life and uses dialogue to subtly define and differentiate characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "perfect fidelity of her dialogue and the subtle definition of her characters are fused into a vitally compelling substance." Example: Fannie Hurst's 'Ice Water, PI—!' Warning: excellent dialogue can be undermined by lack of economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delicacy and tenderness in structure (dreamlike or episodic forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handles delicate, dreamlike, or episodic structures with such delicacy and tenderness that the sequence of images remains memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "succession of dream pictures... so delicately woven, and so tenderly touched with beauty, that they will not easily be forgotten." Example: 'Little Selves.' Anti-pattern: structural accident that cannot be repeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative persuasion of reality; mystical substance and rhythmical progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Conveys mystical or elusive subject-matter convincingly, with lucid insight and a rhythmical progression that sustains reader engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "imaginative persuasion of reality... its frankly mystical substance... the atmosphere is very completely realized, and the story has a rhythmical progression that fascinates me." Example: 'The Sun Chaser.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive individuality of literary style
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows a remarkable, individual literary style—distinctive voice and manner—which marks the writer as notable and promising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "remarkable distinction and individuality in literary style." Example: Walter J. Muilenburg's stories. Editorial value: distinctiveness may predict future recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness to the author's aim / judge by author's goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates a story by how successfully it attains the specific goal the author set for it, rather than by an external checklist alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "Accepting the slightness of its texture, I prefer to judge it by the goal which the author set himself, and by this standard it does not fail." Example: 'The Big Stranger on Dorchester Heights.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint in climaxes; avoidance of accentuated climaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Eschews melodramatic or accentuated climaxes in favor of restrained spiritual or emotional climaxes that achieve a quieter but more powerful effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "instinct for avoiding accentuated climaxes of event. For this reason his spiritual climaxes are all the more overwhelmingly real." Example: Rosenblatt's 'The Menorah.' Anti-pattern: seeking spectacle over subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal control and mastery of dramatic fulfillment
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits severe regard for form and shapes difficult situations into a masterpiece of dramatic fulfilment through disciplined technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "With severe regard for form, her imagination shapes a situation of extreme difficulty in handling into a masterpiece of dramatic fulfilment." Example: Elsie Singmaster's 'Penance.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling sentimental types without mawkishness; selective editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals with sentimental types or subject matter honestly but selects and edits material so as not to become mawkish or over-emphatic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "Dealing with sentimental types and yet avoiding sentimentality... Their defect is a lack of economy and selective power." Example: Fannie Hurst; scoring note: control of sentiment often hinges on selective omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contrast to reveal finer grain of character
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses contrasts—in situation, behavior, or descriptive detail—to reveal nuanced aspects of character and moral texture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "the power of contrast is permitted to reveal the finer grain in a woman's character." Example: 'An Awkward Turn.' Practical tip: contrast can function as a test of readers' perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift of selection / freshness of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits an admirable gift of selection—choosing the right small details—and a fresh vision that reanimates familiar material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "The gift of selection is admirable. The freshness of vision which she brings to familiar substance is only to be found in the work of a very fine artist." Example: Alice Brown's stories. Scoring note: selection distinguishes strong practitioners of the short form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing through minimal action to reveal passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduces outward action to an essential minimum so that passion, desire, or inner life is revealed in an intense, arrested instant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "Here action is reduced to an essential minimum in order that passion may be revealed in an eternal instant arrested through half-realized aspirations and desires." Example: 'The Band.' Anti-pattern: overplotting that diffuses emotional focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial vividness; willingness to be ruthless to convey reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjures vivid, often brutal pictorial detail when necessary to convey the reality and imaginative force of the subject—even at the cost of ruthlessness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted phrasing: "The vivid pictorial quality of Mr. Brooks's narrative is appalling in its ruthless brutality... and the story rises to high moments of imaginative spiritual power." Example: 'The Belgian.' Caution: such brutality should serve a moral or artistic purpose, not shock alone.
